General mathematical proofComplete ambient components give the required independenceThe    main note defines each vertex of  $K$  from a complete connected component of the ambient graph  $A$ . Its “connected blocks” are the connected components of  $K$ , including isolated vertices.Let  $W_j$  be the union of ambient vertices belonging to  $K_j$ , and let  $I_j$  be its candidate indices. Then:Every ambient edge has both endpoints in one  $W_j$ .Every replacement has both endpoints in one  $W_j$ .The sets  $I_j$  partition the candidate list.Every combination of local candidate subsets is allowed by the fixed-list problem.For a global subset  $S$ , put  $S_j=S\cap I_j$ ,  $A_j=A[W_j]$ , and  $U_j=U\cap W_j$ . Then
$$A[U_S]
=
\bigsqcup_j
A_j\!\left[
  \left(U_j\setminus\{x_i:i\in S_j\}\right)
  \cup\{y_i:i\in S_j\}
\right].$$
Maximum matching number is additive over this vertex-disjoint union. A matching restricts to local matchings, and local maximum matchings unite into a global matching. Therefore
$$\nu(A[U_S])=\sum_j \nu(A_j[(U_j)_{S_j}]),
\qquad
|S|=\sum_j |S_j|.$$
Both directions of the feasible-choice correspondence hold, so the exact frontier is precisely
$$F(t)=
\min_{\substack{0\le t_j\le q_j\\ \sum_jt_j=t}}
\sum_j F_j(t_j).$$
This establishes the min-plus convolution without a relaxation or hidden compatibility condition. Matching edges, ambient vertices, and candidate labels belong to only one local problem. Convolution overhead and the maximum-rank exponentFor positive-candidate blocks, let  $Q_{j-1}$  be the number of candidates in earlier positive blocks. Their sequential convolution work is bounded by
$$\sum_j (Q_{j-1}+1)(q_j+1).$$
Expanding gives a pairwise cross term, a sum of earlier budgets, and linear terms. In particular,
$$\sum_jQ_{j-1}q_j
=
\frac{q^2-\sum_jq_j^2}{2},$$
and there are at most  $q$  positive-candidate blocks. Consequently the total is  $O(q^2)$ .A block with  $q_j=0$  has one fixed-cost row. Its cost is retained.
